title: The Thorn of Ironhollow Revisited
premise: Jude Winterbourne, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent their whole life in Ironhollow, a valley where magic cannot follow — until the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, and the outside world pours in. Dragged from their home by a fugitive star-priest named Sera and a disgraced knight, Jude learns that the usurper Veyra sold her own soul to the court beneath the mountain to seize the throne, and that the stolen soul is the key to restoring the stars. Pursued by Veyra's armies across the free cities, Jude must master a magic that has never worked inside them before, choosing between the loyalty they owe their found family and the truth about who sold the wards in the first place. In the end, Jude trades their oath — the last binding of their name — to buy back the soul beneath the mountain, extinguishing their own swordspeaking forever but reigniting the stars; the free cities hold, the found family scatters into new lives, and Jude returns to Ironhollow as an ordinary person at last.
about_author: A. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who grew up in a mining town ringed by mountains and never stopped imagining what lived under them. They write fantasy about stubborn people in small places whose choices turn out to matter enormously.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the eve of the harvest vigil, every star above Ironhollow vanishes at once, and the border wards — silent for two hundred years — shatter like glass. Jude feels their oath-bound sword hum for the first time. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder, the safe world ending quietly.

chapters.title: Refugees at the Wardstone
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Frightened villagers demand answers at the broken wardstone; Jude, as last swordspeaker, is expected to fix what cannot be fixed. A wounded stranger, Sera, collapses at the threshold carrying a shard of fallen starlight. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility, the weight of being 'the last.'

chapters.title: What Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Recovering in Jude's cottage, Sera explains the valley's secret: Ironhollow was built to hide something from the court beneath the mountain, and now that it's exposed, hunters are coming. She won't say what's hidden. Emotional beat: wary trust forming between strangers.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A rider arrives — Dame Corvel Ashgrave, once the queen's shield, now branded traitor — pursued by the usurper Veyra's outriders. Corvel brings proof: Veyra sold her soul to the under-court to take the throne, and the stolen soul is why the stars died. Emotional beat: the past arriving with blood on its boots.

chapters.title: The First Skirmish
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Veyra's soldiers reach the valley. Jude draws the oath-sword and discovers their swordspeaking works for the first time outside ritual — words become edges. They win, barely, and the village burns anyway. Emotional beat: power and grief arriving together.

chapters.title: Leaving Ironhollow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The survivors vote: some stay to rebuild, but Jude, Sera, and Corvel must carry the star-shard to the free cities before Veyra's armies arrive. Jude crosses the wardline and feels magic flood into them like cold water. Emotional beat: exile as both wound and liberation.

chapters.title: The Road of Broken Bells
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. The three travel through war-ravaged countryside where temple bells have been melted down for Veyra's cannons. Corvel confesses she served Veyra once and failed to stop the soul-selling. Emotional beat: guilt shared is burden halved — the found family begins.

chapters.title: Freehold of Marrowgate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The free city of Marrowgate, all canals and candle markets, offers brief refuge — and a black market where someone recognizes the star-shard and sends word to Veyra. Jude meets Tam, a pickpocket orphan who becomes an unlikely guide. Emotional beat: beauty persisting inside danger.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain (A Story)
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, told around a fire. Sera reveals she was once an acolyte of the under-court and fled when she learned what Veyra had purchased: not just a soul, but the binding that holds the stars alight. To restore them, the soul must be reclaimed in person. Emotional beat: myth becoming map.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Candle Market
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Veyra's agents ambush the group in Marrowgate; Tam sells their location to buy food for the street children, then repents and helps them escape through the sewers. Corvel is gravely wounded holding the rearguard. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and imperfectly redeemed.

chapters.title: The Quiet Camp
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hiding in the hills while Corvel feverishly heals, Jude and Sera keep watch and speak honestly for the first time — about fear, about wanting a life after all this. Jude admits the sword frightens them more than the enemy does. Emotional beat: tenderness in the eye of the storm.

chapters.title: Veyra's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. A herald finds them: Veyra offers Jude full pardon, restoration of Ironhollow, and a place at court if they surrender the star-shard. Jude refuses, but the offer plants a poisonous seed — the valley could be saved without the quest. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Muster
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Reaching the city of Aurelspire, they find the free cities bickering, unwilling to unite against Veyra. Jude speaks before the council — not as a hero but as a witness to burned villages — and moves them to arm, barely. Emotional beat: ordinary words doing extraordinary work.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Wards
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Deciphering the star-shard, Sera discovers the wards didn't fail — they were sold, and the seller was Ironhollow's own founder: Jude's ancestor, who hid the valley to protect the very soul Veyra later bought. Jude's inheritance is complicity. Emotional beat: truth cutting deeper than any blade.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. Jude, furious at generations of lies, nearly abandons the quest to go home; Corvel talks them down by admitting her own failures. Tam returns with news: Veyra's army marches on Aurelspire in ten days. Emotional beat: anger burning down into resolve.

chapters.title: Descent Through the Rootways
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The only path to the under-court runs through the Rootways, ancient tunnels beneath the mountains. The party descends past sleeping things and singing stone, Sera navigating by memory of her old faith. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage, going down into the dark on purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the under-court's gate, the toll is a memory apiece. Jude gives up their mother's face; Corvel gives up her knighting day; Sera gives up her reason for fleeing. They enter hollowed-out, holding each other's memories instead. Emotional beat: sacrifice as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain (The Truth)
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the obsidian court, Jude confronts the thing that bought Veyra's soul — and learns it doesn't want worship, only company; it has been alone since the stars were lit. Negotiation begins, dangerous and strange. Emotional beat: horror softening into terrible empathy.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The court will return the soul only for an equal binding: an oath freely given. Jude realizes their swordspeaker's oath — the last one — is the only coin of sufficient weight. Above, Veyra's army reaches Aurelspire's walls; time runs out in both worlds. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Stars Relit
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. As Aurelspire's defenders break against Veyra's first assault, Jude surrenders their oath beneath the mountain. The stars ignite overhead mid-battle; Veyra's soldiers, seeing their usurper's bargain voided, waver and rout. Emotional beat: triumph and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. The cost is tallied: Jude can no longer speak steel, Veyra is taken alive to face the cities' judgment, and the under-court, given the returned soul's warmth, begins to change. The found family tends each other's missing memories, telling stories to fill the gaps. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing a table.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude walks back into Ironhollow — no longer swordspeaker, just a person — where the rebuilt village and Tam's adopted street children await. Sera stays; Corvel rides east to help refound the shattered orders. Jude hangs the silent sword above the door and steps into an ordinary, hard-won life. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
